title: Unescaped link ids can refresh or enumerate the wrong link
reasoning: insertLinkedValue writes linkId directly into an XML attribute without escaping or validating it, while refreshLinkedValue locates links by raw substring search. If linkId contains XML-significant characters the generated document XML can become malformed. If linkId is a prefix of another id, refreshLinkedValue can match the wrong content control because it does not require the full w:tag value to equal the requested id. listLinkIds also only recognizes lowercase hex/dash ids, so links created with other ids can be inserted and refreshed but will not be reported as present.
reproduction: Call insertLinkedValue with linkId "abc" and later refreshLinkedValue(docx, "ab", "new") on a document whose tag contains docgit-link:abc; the substring search can select that control even though "ab" is not the stored id. Similarly, a linkId containing a quote can be written into w:val without escaping.
recommendation: Constrain link ids to the same identifier grammar everywhere, preferably before insertion and refresh, or XML-escape the attribute value and parse/match the exact w:tag value instead of using substring search.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided for this feature, and the owned files contain no tests covering malformed ids, prefix ids, or listLinkIds consistency.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add word-links tests that inserting invalid ids is rejected or escaped, refreshing a prefix id does not mutate a longer-id link, and listLinkIds returns every id that insertLinkedValue accepts.
minimumFixScope: Update packages/core/src/links/word-links.ts link-id handling in insertLinkedValue, refreshLinkedValue, and listLinkIds so they share one exact id contract.
